These elements align with the regulatory topic of benchmarks and measurement methodologies for accuracy/performance. However, the retrieved fragments do not address key elements of Article 15(2): there is no reference to cooperating with external stakeholders or metrology/benchmarking authorities, no requirement to encourage or participate in the development of benchmarks or measurement methodologies across stakeholders, and no explicit coverage of robustness measurement methodologies. Therefore this internal policy is a partial match (it covers internal benchmarking and performance measurement) but is missing the external cooperation and encouragement aspects mandated by the Article. A human Compliance Analyst should review and confirm whether existing internal procedures need extension to include external stakeholder cooperation and formal engagement in benchmark/methodology development.

Business units are responsible for monitoring the ongoing performance of models
under their ownership against the metrics agreed at validation, and escalating
material performance degradation to the Model Risk Function outside of the

retrieved_fragments.policy_title: Acme Bank Model Risk Management Standard
retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
All Tier 1 and Tier 2 models are subject to a formal revalidation exercise on an
**annual basis**, repeating the initial validation steps in Section 3 against
current data and current model performance.

retrieved_fragments.policy_title: Acme Bank Model Risk Management Standard
retrieved_fragments.excerpt:
Prior to first use, every model must undergo independent validation by the Model
Risk Function, covering:

- Conceptual soundness of the model design
- Data quality and representativeness of training/validation data
- Outcome analysis and benchmark comparison
- Identification of known limitations and boundary conditions
